# PCM quality: 0.6.0

**DRAFT.** Measured with dsd-measure 0.1.1 and not final: the published comparison is re-run with the pinned releases (see notes).

pysacd 0.6.0's PCM output against 0.5.5's, measured with dsd-measure 0.1.1 (commit d234b7a) on the same machine with the same inputs, from the [pinned suite](../../suites/pysacd.toml). A change larger than the bound is flagged.

**Conclusion.** 4 figure(s) of 0.6.0 are worse than 0.5.5 by more than the suite's repeatability; this blocks the release unless DECISIONS.md explains and accepts it.

## Notes

- Inputs: identical for both versions (SHA-256 of every file fed to pysacd); null-test source SHA-256 `128f6ecb97a4060a`.
- Repeatability: largest spread over three dither draws of the candidate, per figure: sinad 0.10 dB, thdn 0.10 dB, noise 0.02 dB, alias 0.11 dB.
- Null depth: stereo FLAC 88.2 kHz 124.1 dB (two dither draws of the candidate: 124.3 dB); stereo FLAC 176.4 kHz 127.3 dB (two dither draws of the candidate: 127.4 dB); 5.1 WAV 88.2 kHz 124.1 dB (two dither draws of the candidate: 124.4 dB); 5.1 WAV 176.4 kHz 127.3 dB (two dither draws of the candidate: 127.4 dB).
- Candidate: the 0.6.0 release branch with dsd2pcm 0.1.2 built from its main branch before the 0.1.2 tag; Linux x86-64, Ryzen AI 9 HX 370, Fedora 45 container, one worker thread.
- The 88.2 kHz SINAD and THD+N change is not dither: 0.5.5 with two other dither draws reads 127.81 and 127.81 dB (stereo), against 127.24 to 127.27 dB for 0.6.0. The noise floor with no signal is unchanged, so the added noise grows with the signal level; it is about 136 dB below a 0 dB SACD tone.
- Final when re-run with released dsd2pcm 0.1.2 and dsd-measure 0.1.2 (output word-length detection), with bounds re-derived on that pin.
